key_insight: ShortCoder combines external code knowledge with syntax-aware representations to compress and restructure code generation so that models emit fewer tokens for the same program, reducing inference passes and compute cost.
problem_solved: LLM-based code generation is token-inefficient: every generated token requires a full inference step and large context retention, causing high latency, memory use, and cost for producing long or repetitive code.
method: Knowledge augmentation: inject retrieved or pre-learned code patterns, API usage, and idioms to raise the semantic abstraction level the model needs to generate.
Syntax-aware compression: convert code to compact, syntax-preserving representations (e.g., AST-driven tokenization/macros) so that common constructs map to fewer tokens.
Decoder-friendly integration: align the compact representations with the model decoder (scaffolding/caching) to reduce per-token inference and enable multi-token emission of structured blocks.
impact: By cutting token counts and inference passes, ShortCoder lowers latency and compute cost for code generation systems, making LLM-based coding tools faster, cheaper, and more feasible on constrained hardware or at production scale.
